claim: F_q[T], exact integers (q = 7, 13; 2452 row energies, columns up to degree 12). Row energy / diagonal = n + B_coh: n is at most about 1.1 (measured), B_coh is the squared probe signal (Moebius sum of the row weight times the sixth-power count; Bessel inequality proved at dual length 0). Weil targets: exponent <= 1.05 in all 65 + 18 bulk configurations (N >= 2, marks <= 6); 4 to 15 times the diagonal when the dual length exceeds 3N (one case predicted in advance), so (E-K) fails for the target beyond h = 3. Random unimodular, random sign, multiplicative-sign and two-character vectors behave as the targets; mu and a sign twist exceed the diagonal by B_coh; only an aligned vector reaches the Hilbert-Schmidt size. Compensated probe: rescaled term = q^(-lam) part of the marked signal; h > 1 survives; low input unchanged. Reflected completed rows NOT-RUN.

surviving: Model statement only, no statement about zeta: (E-K) is equivalent, to the accuracy of the data, to the power-saving bound for the target's own Moebius sum with the sixth-power weight; true for Weil targets up to dual length 3N, false beyond; not specific to the target among generic vectors.
lesson: A mean-square hypothesis over a row set must be tested against its Bessel part first: the energy is diagonal plus squared signal, so the hypothesis is the conclusion. A random vector always shows the diagonal (mean over phases); operator-norm sizes need an aligned vector as control.
followUp: If the branch is kept: completed rows (cube part) for one target, and one more point with dual length above 3N at N >= 2 to measure growth in the degree. Otherwise close (E-K) as circular and route the E-K proof lane to the coherent term.
